# Wisdom of Solomon Chapter 1 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Wisdom 1 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/WIS_001_page_001.jpg

---

**1:1** Love righteousness, you who judge the earth; think of the Lord in goodness, and seek him in simplicity of heart.

**1:2** Because he is found by those who do not test him, and he is made manifest to those who do not distrust him.

**1:3** For crooked reasonings separate from God, and his power, when tested, exposes the foolish.

**1:4** Because wisdom will not enter into a soul that plots evil, nor will it dwell in a body enslaved to sin.

**1:5** For the holy spirit of discipline flees deceit, and withdraws from thoughts that are without understanding, and is put to shame when unrighteousness draws near.

**1:6** For wisdom is a spirit that loves humanity, and will not acquit a blasphemer of his lips; because God is witness of his inmost parts, and a true overseer of his heart, and a hearer of his tongue.

**1:7** Because the spirit of the Lord has filled the world, and that which holds all things together has knowledge of every sound.

**1:8** Therefore no one who speaks unjust things will be unnoticed, nor will justice, when it punishes, pass him by.

**1:9** For the reasonings of the ungodly will be examined, and the report of his words will come to the Lord, for the proof of his lawless deeds.

**1:10** Because a jealous ear hears all things, and the sound of grumblings is not hidden.

**1:11** Therefore guard yourselves from useless grumbling, and keep your tongue from slander; because no secret word goes forth without result, and a lying mouth destroys the soul.

**1:12** Do not seek death in the error of your life, nor bring upon yourselves destruction by the works of your hands.

**1:13** Because God did not make death, nor does he take delight in the destruction of the living.

**1:14** For he created all things that they might exist, and the generative forces of the world are wholesome, and there is no destructive poison in them, nor is the kingdom of Hades upon the earth.

**1:15** For righteousness is immortal.

**1:16** But the ungodly, by their hands and their words, called death to themselves; accounting it a friend, they wore themselves away, and they made a covenant with it, because they are worthy to belong to its portion.

---

*EMET rendering preserves Greek philosophical vocabulary: dikaiosynē (righteousness), athanasia (immortality), sophia (wisdom). The spirit of the Lord (pneuma kyriou) fills the cosmos — a Stoic resonance. "Jealous ear" (ous zēloun) rendered literally. Verse 15 stands as a complete theological thesis.*
